accepted.s: The institution of Ombudsman was first established in which country in 1809?
accepted.x: The Ombudsman institution was first set up in Sweden in 1809. Sweden’s 1766 law is associated with the right to information, not the origin of the Ombudsman institution.
accepted.tq: Use the date-place pair and distinguish it from the nearby 1766 Swedish fact.
accepted.sec: Ombudsman idea - Sweden, Indian equivalent; who coined 'Lokpal'  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Indian equivalents of the Ombudsman at the Union and State levels respectively?
accepted.x: Lokpal is the Ombudsman institution at the Union level, while Lokayukta performs the corresponding role at the State level.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two similar terms by matching them with Union and State levels.
accepted.sec: Ombudsman idea - Sweden, Indian equivalent; who coined 'Lokpal'  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which State was the first in India to establish a Lokayukta?
accepted.x: Maharashtra was the first State to establish a Lokayukta, in 1971.
accepted.tq: Separate the first institution from the first law by focusing on the verb ‘establish’.
accepted.sec: Ombudsman idea - Sweden, Indian equivalent; who coined 'Lokpal'  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the declaration of assets under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas law:
1. The original law required declaration of assets and liabilities of the public servant, spouse and dependent children.
2. The declaration was required within 30 days of entering office.
3. The 2016 amendment prescribed the form and manner of declaration directly in the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 2016 amendment provided that the form and manner would be prescribed by the Central Government; it did not place the prescription in the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Reject the wrong-authority trap in statement 3 and retain the two precise statutory details.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas (Amendment) Act 2016 - asset declaration  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What was the principal change made by the Lokpal and Lokayuktas (Amendment) Act, 2016 concerning asset declarations?
o: It authorised the Central Government to prescribe the form and manner of declaration.
It made declaration of assets optional for public servants.
It abolished declaration by dependent children.
It transferred the power to prescribe the form to the State Governments.
accepted.x: The 2016 amendment retained the obligation to declare assets and liabilities but authorised the Central Government to prescribe the form and manner of declaration.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise institutional power instead of confusing amendment with abolition or transfer.
accepted.sec: Lokpal and Lokayuktas (Amendment) Act 2016 - asset declaration  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Lokayuktas in the States is correct?
o: Jurisdiction, coverage of the Chief Minister and qualifications may differ from State to State.
The Act prescribes an identical jurisdiction and identical coverage of the Chief Minister for every State.
Only Union Territories may modify the jurisdiction of their Lokayuktas.
The Act requires every State to adopt the Maharashtra model without modification.
accepted.x: There is no uniform model under which every State has identical jurisdiction, Chief Minister coverage or qualifications. These features differ from State to State.
accepted.tq: Avoid the absolute ‘identical’ and ‘without modification’ traps in a federal arrangement.
accepted.sec: Mandate on states to set up Lokayuktas - time limit  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which State was the first to pass a law relating to the Lokayukta?
accepted.x: Odisha was the first State to pass a Lokayukta law, in 1970. The institution in Odisha came into existence later, in 1983.
accepted.tq: Distinguish ‘first to pass a law’ from ‘first to establish an institution’.
accepted.sec: Mandate on states to set up Lokayuktas - time limit  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following States in chronological order of the year of their Lokayukta Acts:
A. Rajasthan
B. Andhra Pradesh
C. Bihar
D. Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: The years are Rajasthan—1973, Bihar—1974, Uttar Pradesh—1975 and Andhra Pradesh—1983. Therefore, the order is A, C, D, B.
accepted.tq: Place the dated entries first and then verify the middle pair carefully.
accepted.sec: Mandate on states to set up Lokayuktas - time limit  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: By 2013, Lokayuktas had been established in how many States and Union Territories respectively?
accepted.x: By 2013, 21 States and one Union Territory, Delhi, had Lokayuktas.
accepted.tq: Read the State and Union Territory counts as a combined numerical pair.
accepted.sec: Mandate on states to set up Lokayuktas - time limit  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CBI supervision — Director of Inquiry of the State Government
accepted.x: The Lokpal’s Inquiry Wing is headed by a Director of Inquiry. The Prosecution Wing is headed by a Director of Prosecution.
accepted.tq: Match each wing with its exact head and reject the swapped designations.
accepted.sec: Powers - inquiry wing, prosecution wing, CBI superintendence, attachment of property  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Inquiry Wing of the Lokpal conducts preliminary inquiry into offences under the:
accepted.x: The Inquiry Wing conducts preliminary inquiries into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory subject of the inquiry rather than the name of the investigating wing alone.
accepted.sec: Powers - inquiry wing, prosecution wing, CBI superintendence, attachment of property  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers associated with the Lokpal:
1. The Prosecution Wing files cases before the Special Court.
2. The Lokpal exercises superintendence and direction over the CBI in cases referred by it.
3. The Lokpal may summon persons and requisition records in the manner of a civil court.
4. Property acquired by corrupt means can be attached and confiscated even while prosecution is pending.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Lokpal’s framework includes prosecution before the Special Court, specified CBI superintendence, civil-court powers and attachment or confiscation of tainted property during pending prosecution.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against a distinct power before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Powers - inquiry wing, prosecution wing, CBI superintendence, attachment of property  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The recently established Inquiry Wing of the Lokpal has three Superintendents of Police dealing with which combination of areas?
o: General, economic and banking, and cyber
General, political and constitutional, and cyber
accepted.x: The three SP-level areas are general matters, economic and banking matters, and cyber matters.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact three-part administrative classification rather than substituting neighbouring fields.
accepted.sec: Powers - inquiry wing, prosecution wing, CBI superintendence, attachment of property  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function or power associated with the Lokpal under the stated framework?
o: Conducting elections to State Legislative Assemblies
Attaching property acquired through corrupt means
Recommending transfer, suspension and disciplinary action
accepted.x: Conducting elections to State Legislative Assemblies is not a Lokpal function. The other three are among the powers or associated actions of the Lokpal.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated constitutional function while retaining the listed anti-corruption powers.
accepted.sec: Powers - inquiry wing, prosecution wing, CBI superintendence, attachment of property  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The report of the Inquiry Wing after a reference is ordinarily required within:
accepted.x: The Inquiry Wing is required to submit its report within 60 days after a reference.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the 60-day report period from the separate 90-day preliminary inquiry period.
accepted.sec: Time limits for inquiry and investigation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the preliminary inquiry under the Lokpal framework, consider the following statements:
1. It is ordinarily to be completed within 90 days.
2. It may be extended by a further 90 days.
3. Extension does not require recording reasons in writing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: A preliminary inquiry ordinarily has a 90-day limit and may be extended by another 90 days. Reasons for the extension must be recorded in writing, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Spot the negative requirement trap: written reasons are necessary for extension.
accepted.sec: Time limits for inquiry and investigation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The investigation period under the Lokpal framework is:
o: Six months, extendable by six months
Nine months, extendable by three months
Three months, extendable by three months
One year, extendable by one year
accepted.x: Investigation is to be completed within six months and may be extended by a further six months.
accepted.tq: Keep the base period and permissible extension as a matched pair.
accepted.sec: Time limits for inquiry and investigation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The trial of a case by the Special Court is to be completed within one year, and the period may be extended up to a maximum of:
accepted.x: The Special Court trial is to be completed within one year, with extension permitted up to two years.
accepted.tq: Separate the normal trial period from the maximum extended period.
accepted.sec: Time limits for inquiry and investigation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following States includes the Chief Minister within the jurisdiction of its Lokayukta according to the stated classification?
accepted.x: The Chief Minister is included within the Lokayukta’s jurisdiction in Himachal Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan are among the States listed as excluding the Chief Minister.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between included and excluded State groups using one positive example.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta's jurisdiction over CM, ministers, legislators - state-wise  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following States is listed as excluding the Chief Minister from the jurisdiction of its Lokayukta?
accepted.x: Odisha is among the States listed as excluding the Chief Minister. Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh are listed among the States including the Chief Minister.
accepted.tq: Use the exclusion list directly and avoid reversing the two jurisdictional groups.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta's jurisdiction over CM, ministers, legislators - state-wise  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
In which of the following States are Members of the Legislative Assembly included within the jurisdiction of the Lokayukta according to the stated classification?
1. Andhra Pradesh
2. Himachal Pradesh
3. Gujarat
4. Uttar Pradesh
5. Assam
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: MLAs are listed as covered in Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Assam. Thus, all five statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Build the answer from the complete inclusion list rather than inferring from Chief Minister coverage.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta's jurisdiction over CM, ministers, legislators - state-wise  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the investigation subjects under Section 7 of the Rajasthan Lokayukta and Deputy Lokayukta Act, 1973?
accepted.x: Sexual harassment, caste discrimination and violence are not among the investigation subjects listed under the stated Rajasthan provision. Corruption is the core subject associated with the Lokayukta framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the exception by separating the specifically excluded social offences from the anti-corruption mandate.
accepted.sec: Lokayukta's jurisdiction over CM, ministers, legislators - state-wise  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended:
o: A Lokayukta in every State and a Lokpal at the Centre
A Central Vigilance Commission in every State and a Lokpal only in Union Territories
Only a State Lokayukta, without any institution at the Centre
A separate constitutional court for corruption cases
accepted.x: The First Administrative Reforms Commission, chaired by Morarji Desai, recommended a Lokayukta in every State and a Lokpal at the Centre.
accepted.tq: Match the recommending body with the complete two-level institutional proposal.
accepted.sec: Origin - body that first recommended state Lokayuktas  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The First Administrative Reforms Commission, which recommended Lokayuktas in the States and a Lokpal at the Centre, functioned during:
accepted.x: The First Administrative Reforms Commission functioned from 1966 to 1970 and was chaired by Morarji Desai.
accepted.tq: Test the commission’s date range separately from its recommendation and chairperson.
accepted.sec: Origin - body that first recommended state Lokayuktas  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Karnataka Lokayukta model?
o: It was created under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1971, without a police wing.
It was established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 2013, with no investigative role.
It functions only as an advisory body under the Central Lokpal.
It was created under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, and has its own Lokayukta Police wing.
accepted.x: The Karnataka Lokayukta was established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, and has its own Lokayukta Police wing.
accepted.tq: Combine the exact year with the distinctive institutional feature to reject near-date traps.
accepted.sec: Karnataka Lokayukta model and its major reports  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report of 2011 was associated with:
accepted.x: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report was prepared under Justice N. Santosh Hegde in 2011.
accepted.tq: Match the report with its author while avoiding confusion with other Lokayukta-related names.
accepted.sec: Karnataka Lokayukta model and its major reports  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the consequences associated with the Bellary illegal iron ore mining report?
o: Abolition of the Karnataka Lokayukta Police wing
Arrest of former minister G. Janardhana Reddy
accepted.x: The report led to the Chief Minister’s resignation, the arrest of former minister G. Janardhana Reddy, cancellation of mining leases and recovery of thousands of crores. It did not abolish the Lokayukta Police wing.
accepted.tq: Find the invented institutional consequence among several genuine effects of the report.
accepted.sec: Karnataka Lokayukta model and its major reports  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Karnataka Lokayukta Police trapped Shirahatti BJP MLA Chandru Lamani while allegedly accepting a bribe of:
accepted.x: Chandru Lamani was trapped by the Karnataka Lokayukta Police while taking a ₹5 lakh bribe.
accepted.tq: Test the exact amount attached to the named person and operation.
accepted.sec: Karnataka Lokayukta model and its major reports  [GROUP-II]
